This picks up from an accepted RCA at `docs/specs/<KEY>.html` on the `<KEY>-rca` branch; work on that branch (rename it `<KEY>` when you first commit code). The harness under `.repro/<KEY>/` is the acceptance test: it fails before your change and passes after it, against the app you run from `.prepcook/scripts.toml`. The login stays in the environment. Nothing under `.repro/` is ever staged.

`<target>` is the branch the work merges into: the target of the branch's pull request when one exists (ask `gh` or `glab`, whichever your host uses), else the remote's default branch — `git symbolic-ref --short refs/remotes/origin/HEAD`, usually `origin/main`. "Pull request" means a merge request too, on GitLab.

Ticket: $ARGUMENTS. Read it through your tracker's MCP before anything else — its description, its comments, its attachments and any recording linked from it (for Jira, the Atlassian MCP: `getJiraIssue`, then the comments and attachments). `<KEY>` below is that ticket's key.

Read the approved root-cause analysis at docs/specs/<KEY>.html in full before touching code. The reproduction it records is the acceptance test: fix the mechanism it isolated with the smallest change that achieves the behaviour the RCA specifies, and nothing else. Scope by behaviour, not by file — the files the RCA names are where to start, not the boundary of the change; if the mechanism runs through a second site (a second caller, a second creator, a second entry point), the fix covers it. Do not refactor around the fix. Add the regression tests the RCA calls for, and run the relevant test suite until green. Prefer targeted tests over full builds: run only the tests that cover your change. Your app is the acceptance environment: rebuild and restart it from this branch and run the harness from `.repro/<KEY>/` against it until it passes, then run the manifest's `test` command once before you hand on — the check the orchestrator runs before a pull request opens. Flag any deviation from the RCA explicitly.

Anything long-running runs in the foreground under `timeout` (raise the Bash tool's timeout to match).

Write evergreen comments: a comment must make sense to someone reading the file cold, with no ticket, pull request or git history in front of them. Document the current behaviour and the constraint behind it, never the change that produced it — BAD: `// New validation per BUG-1234` or `// Previously returned null; now returns empty list`; GOOD: `// Reject >1MB; larger payloads crash the downstream parser` or `// Returns empty list (never null) so callers can iterate unconditionally`. Temporal narrative belongs in the commit message and the pull request description.

When the fix changes anything a user can see, capture the evidence while the change is still fresh — a reviewer should not have to run the branch to see a visual fix. Capture against the running app at `$PREPCOOK_APP_URL` with Playwright (its bundled Chromium; `$PREPCOOK_CHROMIUM_PATH` when set), logging in with `$PREPCOOK_TEST_USER_EMAIL` and `$PREPCOOK_TEST_USER_PASSWORD` from the environment — never print, log or commit them. Wait for `networkidle` before reading the DOM or clicking anything, and give the app a settle beat after each interaction: a screenshot of a half-rendered page is evidence of nothing. Find selectors by reconnaissance rather than guesswork — capture the rendered DOM first, choose selectors from what is actually there, then act; a selector you assumed will fail silently and leave you debugging the harness instead of the defect. Screenshot the broken state and the fixed state at the viewport the ticket reports (1440x900 when it says nothing), writing them to .repro/<KEY>/before.png and after.png — under .repro/, which is excluded through .git/info/exclude (add the line if it is missing) and is never committed: evidence goes on the pull request, not into the branch. Rebuild and restart the app after your change (the manifest's `build`, then `start`), so the "after" is the fixed build. Get the "before" by reinstating the defect in the working tree, rebuilding and restarting, capturing, then reverting it and restarting again, and say so when you report it. Annotate the measurements the diagnosis rested on — getBoundingClientRect, computed style, whatever the defect was measured in — onto the page before capturing, so the image carries evidence rather than an impression. When the real thing cannot be captured (the app does not stand up, or the state needs data the seed cannot hold), capture the closest thing you can — the component in isolation, say — and state plainly what the screenshot is not. List the paths in your completion summary.

Stop here once the harness passes and the tests are green: commit, run `/prepcook-self-review` here, then `/prepcook-review` in a fresh session, and `/prepcook-mr` after it.
